text:
song: Heads-up — saw a cluster of small, transient OOMs on 32GB nodes during the afternoon load test. Pattern looks like: high kv-cache pressure + many short batched requests, then a tail spike.

maria: Can you paste the tails of the profile/logs? Is it fragmentation or sudden large allocs?

song: paste of trimmed log: ```
[2026-02-18T15:22:10Z] serve: batch=12 seq=128 model=gptx quant=8 
cudaMalloc 0.49GB failed -> OOM
free_total=1.1GB free_largest=280MB fragmented=65%
active_alloc_count=324 free_small_chunks=142
```

kevin: That free_largest vs free_total gap screams fragmentation. We're hitting many small scratchpads and logits buffers, then a new activation/chunk needs contiguous >300MB and fails.

dana: Do we have recent changes to the batching heuristic or kernel selection that increase short-lived allocations? I recall a kernel patch last week that allocates per-request scratchpad for fused attention.

song: Yes, kernel roll 2026-02-17 added an eager workspace per request to avoid repeated kernel calls. It reduced latency for large batched requests, but seems to regress tail fragmentation on small batches.

prashant: If this is fragmentation, a compaction/merge pass in the tensor pool could help. But full compaction is expensive and may spike latency. We need a heuristic trigger.

maria: Proposal: compact when (fragmented_ratio > 0.5 AND free_small_chunks > 128) OR (allocation_failure && free_total > threshold). That way we don't compaction on low pressure.

kevin: I tried a prototype: trigger_compact if (free_largest < required && free_total >= required + slack && fragmented_ratio > 0.4). Slack=256MB. Pseudocode: ```
if (!alloc_ok && free_total >= req + SLACK && frag_ratio > FRAG_THRESH) compact();
```
Result: prevented 80% of the small OOMs in local sim but increased tail p95 by ~6ms on synthetic large batches.

dana: Tradeoff seems acceptable for 32GB nodes serving latency-sensitive endpoints? We need SLO analysis. Which endpoints saw the regression?

song: Affected mostly chat-stream routes that prefer lower latency. The p95 jump was across the board for that instance class during compaction windows.

prashant: Another idea: prefer in-place reuse by tightening eviction for logits/scratchpad pools. If we avoid creating many small freelists by reusing similar-sized scratchpads via size-bucketing we reduce fragmentation. E.g., max-bucket-delta = 1.15 so we reuse slightly larger buffers rather than creating new ones.

kevin: Yep — size-bucket reuse + low-overhead eager coalescing of adjacent free small chunks reduced frag ratio in my run. We also need to watch KV cache behavior: when we evict KV segments we should try to free contiguous memory ranges not scattered pages. Batch evictions by age can help.

maria: Actionable experiment plan:
- A: implement compact-on-failure heuristic (kevin prototype) and run 24h cluster canary on 32GB (owner: kevin)
- B: implement size-bucket tightening for scratchpad/logits with bucket_delta=1.15 (owner: dana)
- C: add KV eviction coalescing to prefer contiguous blocks (owner: prashant)
- D: add telemetry: record frag_ratio, free_total, free_largest, compaction_events and correlate with p50/p95 latency per-route (owner: song)

kevin: I'll push A as a canary flag in runtime-config: ```
allocator.compact_on_failure = true
allocator.compact_frag_threshold = 0.4
allocator.compact_slack_mb = 256
```
Plan: run for 6h on canary pool first.

dana: For B I'll add bucket metadata and a small fast-path to prefer reuse for +-15% sized buffers. I'll measure CPU overhead; it should be minimal (<1%).

prashant: For C, KV eviction coalescing note: we should avoid increasing tail latency of reads. Do coalescing asynchronously if possible, or piggyback on periodic GC windows.

maria: Let's also add a test harness to synthesize workload: many short chats with kv density high + occasional long chat that induces large activation. Use that to verify OOM frequency and p95 tradeoff.

song: Agreed. Quick preliminary metrics we want: OOM_count, compaction_count, frag_ratio_95, p95_latency_route. If compaction_count correlates with reduced OOM_count and acceptable p95 increase, we keep it.

kevin: I'll create the canary and post results here after 6h. Starting now. @dana @prashant tagging for visibility. :rocket:

infra-bot: Canary cluster deploy started by kevin at 2026-02-18T16:02:45Z (tag: allocator-compact-canary).

maria: Nice. If canary looks good, we should gate the default behind node-size (enable for 32GB, maybe skip 80GB nodes where fragmentation is rarer).

dana: Also add a debug flag to log allocator skyline on compaction events (frag ratio, largest_free before/after) — helpful for postmortem.

song: Thanks all. I'll assemble the experiment checklist and telemetry dashboard metrics. We'll meet next sync if canary shows regressions.

kevin: quick note — when enabling compact_on_failure don't forget to short-circuit compaction if GPU utilization > 85% to avoid stalling busy GPUs.

prashant: Good call. Add that to runtime config: `allocator.compact_max_gpu_util = 0.85`.

maria: Great thread. Feel free to ping infra on escalation if canary OOMs spike. :thumbsup:
